description: The Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative publishes the disclosures of its implementing countries on oil, gas and mining as open data. On 26 September 2026 the open data page reported 56 implementing countries, 780 fiscal years covered and 3.3 trillion US dollars of government revenues disclosed. Summary data, a standardised format, cover financial data, reporting entities (companies and state-owned enterprises), government revenues by revenue stream and project-level payments, coded with HS commodity codes, ISO currencies and the IMF Government Finance Statistics classification so that countries and years can be compared. Data come as the Excel files submitted by countries, bulk downloads per country and an application programming interface, alongside country reports, systematic disclosure pages and the EITI database; the secretariat's open data policy and 2023-2029 data strategy govern publication. Caveats: coverage depends on each country's reporting cycle, often with a lag of two years, and project-level detail varies. For simulation it provides economic and governance data on extractive sites and revenue flows for supply-chain, economic impact and policy evaluation. Related catalogue records include ResourceContracts, which holds the underlying contracts, and the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries.
